subject: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps — FinTechX POC
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechx.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps — FinTechX POC

Hi Alicia / Ben —

Great to meet earlier. Per our call, here’s a concise recap and proposed plan for the POC observability work so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners. I’ve looped in Marissa (SE) and Jonas (AM) to own technical setup and project coordination.

Recap (from today’s discovery):
- Primary goals: validate production-like latency/throughput for a subset of FinTechX request patterns, measure unit cost, and ensure end-to-end observability for troubleshooting/regression detection.
- Scope for POC: 2k–5k requests/day synthetic + 100–500 real production-like requests; 2 model variants (base open model + quantized variant) for fallback comparison; metrics/reporting integration into FinTechX monitoring.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: P95 <= 350ms end-to-end for >90% of test requests (excluding large-document generation flows)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% over a 48h run
- Cost target: < $0.007 / 1k tokens (goal for inference unit economics during POC; will refine by model/config)
- Observability: dashboards + traces live in your monitoring (Datadog/Splunk) showing latency, error rates, model fallback events, and cache hit rates; log export to your S3/BigQuery for audit samples
- Eval: automated eval run comparing sample outputs vs. baseline for quality regressions (pass threshold to be defined by your product team)

Observability deliverables (high level):
- Pre-built dashboard templates: token latency distribution, throughput (tokens/sec), request rate, error rate, model-switch/fallback counts, batching distribution, cache hit ratio, KV-cache miss rate
- Distributed traces mapping: request ID -> inference trace showing model selection, batching time, kernel exec time, network time
- Logging: masked prompt/response sampling, request metadata, trace IDs, and cost-per-request tagging; daily export to S3/GCS or your data warehouse
- Alerts: P99 latency increase, error rate spike, model fallback spike, cost-per-token anomaly

Next steps / timeline (proposed):
- Day 0 (this week): kickoff + access review; FinTechX to share Whitelist IPs and temporary API key scope.
- Week 1: SE integration — instrumentation of headers/tracing and initial dashboard wiring.
- Week 2: Run controlled traffic (synthetic) and collect metrics; iterate on dashboard queries and alert thresholds.
- Week 3: Customer validation runs with production-like traffic; joint review and success criteria sign-off.

Owners:
- FinTechX: Alicia (POC lead) — validate success criteria and provide sample production traces/requests
- Redwood: Marissa (SE) — implement tracing, dashboards, and log export; Jonas (AM) — project coordination and access

Please reply with any edits to the success criteria and what monitoring destination you prefer (Datadog, Splunk, New Relic, or export to S3/BigQuery). Once Alicia confirms, Marissa will share a short observability playbook and a wiring checklist.

Thanks,
Aditya

--
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps — FinTechX POC

Thanks Aditya — this is very helpful. Quick confirmations and a couple of notes from our side: 

Confirmations:
- Success criteria look good as a starting point. We care most about latency for the top-10 user flows (mainly short completions, chat-like requests). P95 <= 350ms is a reasonable initial bar for those flows.
- Observability: we use Datadog for most dashboards and traces. We’d prefer both: native Datadog integration plus daily exports of raw logs to our S3 bucket for compliance.

Notes / asks:
- Can Redwood mask PII from sampled prompts automatically before exporting? We can provide a sample of the fields we consider PII.
- For the quality eval, we’ll share a 200-item prompt set and pass/fail rules (ratio of unacceptable outputs).

Action items from FinTechX:
- I’ll circulate the sample prompt set and provide access to our Datadog sandbox.
- I’ll attach our security questionnaire (we’ll need it filled by your security team) — see attached.

Alicia

Subject: Observability Playbook & Wiring Checklist (FinTechX POC)

Hi Alicia / Ben —

Thanks — I’ll own the Redwood-side observability work. Attached is a short playbook (see attachment stub below) and a checklist to get us started. I’ve also put estimated times for each step.

Attachment stub: redwood_poc_observability_playbook.pdf (3 pages)

High-level wiring checklist:
1) Access & Keys (est. 2h)
   - FinTechX to create a Datadog API key with metric+trace write in your sandbox and an S3 bucket write role for daily exports
   - Provide sample request IDs and a few production-like traces (anonymized)
2) Tracing headers (est. 4h)
   - Add X-Request-ID header and enable pass-through so Redwood traces can be correlated with your front-end.
   - We’ll instrument model calls to return a Redwood-Trace-ID in responses for correlation.
3) Dashboard templates (est. 6h)
   - Token latency histograms (P50/P90/P95/P99), tokens/sec, errors/sec, model_fallback_count, batch_size distribution, cache_hit_ratio
4) Log export (est. 3h + ops)
   - We’ll stream masked sampling (1%) of prompts/responses to S3 daily. We will apply your PII masking rules before export.
5) Alerts & thresholds (est. 2h)
   - Default alerts: P99 > 600ms, error rate > 1%, fallback rate > 5%

POC run plan (instrumentation -> synthetic -> production-like):
- Day 1 (post kickoff): instrumentation complete, basic dashboards live with synthetic traffic
- Day 2–7: synthetic runs and threshold tuning
- Day 8–14: production-like runs and quality evals

Acceptance criteria (concrete checks we'll hand off for sign-off):
- Dashboard shows continuous metrics for the last 72h with <5% missing points
- Traces are linkable: every sampled request in dashboard has a trace with Redwood-Trace-ID and your X-Request-ID
- Logs are exported to S3 and verified by FinTechX security that PII masking rules were applied

Questions for FinTechX:
- Do you have a preferred sampling rate for traces and logs beyond the 1% we suggested?
- Any specific alerting integrations (PagerDuty routing) we should wire now?

Next steps: I’ll schedule a 60-min kickoff with your engineering team (suggest Wed morning). Jonas — can you propose calendar slots?

Thanks,
Marissa

--

Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps — FinTechX POC

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and plenty actionable. Quick confirmations from our infra side: 
- Datadog sandbox is ready; we’ll create an API key scoped for the sandbox and share details in a secure note.
- S3 export is fine — we want daily batched exports and will provide the bucket and role.
- Sampling rate: start with 1% traces and 1% masked prompt/response exports; we’ll increase to 5% if we need more signal in week 2.
- PagerDuty: yes, route critical alerts to our platform escalation policy (I’ll share the integration key).

Next steps from our side:
- Alicia to share sample prompt set and the security questionnaire (I attached a copy here).
- Ben to share Datadog API key + S3 bucket details by EOD Monday.
